Our Heritage

Three Generations. One Continuing Craft.

Wariz Heritage carries forward a Kelantan family tradition shaped across generations, from the artistic foundations of Haji Yusoff Abdullah, through Wan Rabiyah Batik, to the house known today as Wariz Heritage.

First Generation

Haji Yusoff Abdullah

The first generation in our family story, rooted in Kelantan's batik tradition and remembered for a lifelong relationship with art, craft and the visual language of the state. Recognised as Tokoh Budaya and awarded the Anugerah Seni Kelantan.

As documented by ILHAM Gallery and the national Visual Arts curriculum.

Second Generation

Wan Rabiyah Batik

The family's connection to batik continued through Wan Rabiyah Batik, an independent family batik business that carried the craft from artistic inheritance into enterprise.

Third Generation

Wariz Heritage

A contemporary continuation of that inheritance: respecting what came before while creating hand-crafted pieces for today's collectors and wearers. Each design is made as an individual work: drawn once, made once, never repeated.

The Craft

The Hand Is Part of the Work

In hand-crafted batik, no two lines are ever quite the same. Variation is not an imperfection to correct, but evidence of the hand that made it. From the first drawn motif to the final stitch, every stage leaves its trace.

01 · Sketch

The motif is drawn

A design is sketched directly onto plain cloth by hand — never traced from a fixed template.

02 · Canting

Hot wax, by hand

Hot wax follows every line with a canting tool, sealing the cloth beneath from dye.

03 · Dye

Colour, layer by layer

The cloth is dyed in stages, with wax reapplied between each layer to protect what has already been set.

04 · Nglorod

The wax is revealed

Boiling water lifts away the wax, revealing the finished motif in the negative space it protected.

05 · Finishing

One piece, recorded

The finished cloth is inspected, assigned its Wariz Heritage number and entered into the house record — never reprinted, never duplicated.

06 · Cutting the Baju

Cut for the body

Each piece is cut individually to real measurements, allowing the motif and the wearer to shape the final garment.

07 · Fused Lining

Structure, not stiffness

Fused lining gives the garment shape while allowing the hand-crafted motif to remain the focus.

08 · Tailoring

The last hand

Every seam is finished by hand, bringing the cloth from artwork to garment.

Our Exclusive Collection

One Masterpiece Handcrafted

Every Wariz Heritage piece is individually numbered and recorded. Once collected, the exact work is not reproduced; its place remains in the archive.
